stages.label: Clue 1
stages.publicText: Long before porch pumpkins, people in Ireland and Scotland hollowed out a hard root vegetable and carried it as a lantern.

stages.label: Clue 2
stages.publicText: Folklore tied the lantern to Stingy Jack, said to wander with a glowing coal inside.

stages.label: Clue 3
stages.publicText: It is pale, peppery, and older than the American pumpkin custom. What was carved first?

challenges.title: Before the Pumpkin
challenges.hostNotes: Irish and Scottish lanterns were traditionally carved from turnips or other hard roots. Pumpkins became the familiar version in North America.

challenges.title: Calendar Check
challenges.instructions: Fact, or a fright of a fib?
challenges.hostNotes: Halloween is October 31.

challenges.title: Two Different Nights
challenges.instructions: Fact, or a fright of a fib?
challenges.hostNotes: Día de los Muertos is its own tradition, centered on November 1 and 2, ofrendas, and honoring people who have died. It is not another name for Halloween.
challenges.factStatement: Día de los Muertos is just another name for Halloween.

challenges.title: Two Famous Books
challenges.hostNotes: Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein was published in 1818. Bram Stoker’s Dracula was published in 1897.

stages.label: Extra
stages.publicText: A rider with no head. A town that does not sleep well.

challenges.title: Emoji Story
challenges.hostNotes: Washington Irving published The Legend of Sleepy Hollow in 1820.

stages.label: Clue 1

stages.label: Clue 3
stages.publicText: The Spanish name for this offering altar is the answer.

challenges.title: The Offering Table
challenges.hostNotes: An ofrenda is the offering altar for Día de los Muertos, often with photos, food, candles, and cempasúchil marigolds. Speak about the tradition with respect. It is not a Halloween prop.

stages.label: Clue 1
stages.publicText: It belongs to old Irish tradition, at the hinge between autumn and winter.

stages.label: Clue 2
stages.publicText: People marked the end of the harvest and told stories about the boundary between worlds.

stages.label: Clue 3
stages.publicText: Later Halloween customs in Ireland and Scotland are often discussed alongside it. It is not Día de los Muertos, and it is not a pumpkin.

stages.label: Clue 4
stages.publicText: The name is still used for the festival itself. What is it called?

challenges.title: The Last Night of Harvest
challenges.hostNotes: Samhain, the Irish festival at the turn of the harvest season, often linked by historians with later Halloween customs. Pronunciation is roughly “SOW-in.” Do not claim it and Halloween are identical. Wagers are entered by the host.
